title: How far does Aaron walk in two fifths of an hour?
description: A walk of three kilometres in one hour is cut into five equal parts, and two of those parts are taken to find the distance for two fifths of an hour. Keeko then raises a hand with the doubt that five and three should be multiplied at the bottom.
teaching_notes: One idea: to take a fraction of a whole number, divide by the bottom number first and then multiply by the top number. Watch for students who multiply the bottom number by the whole number and keep the top number.

source: Laksh can walk 3 km in 1 hour. How far can he walk in 2/5 of an hour?
video_script.why: The child has added a fraction again and again and now meets a fraction of an hour, where the whole is first cut into equal parts.
video_script.substitution: Two fifths of an hour is two of five equal parts of the hour, so the distance is two of five equal parts of three kilometres.
video_script.anchor: Laksh walks three kilometres in one hour: how far in two fifths of an hour?
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies five by three at the bottom and keeps the two on top, which gives a tiny distance of two fifteenths of a kilometre
video_script.payoff_line: Laksh can walk six fifths of a kilometre in two fifths of an hour

final_answer.spoken: six fifths of a kilometre, that is one and one fifth kilometres

video_script.fraction_reading: one fifth, two fifths, three fifths, six fifths, two fifteenths

names.Laksh: walks 3 km in 1 hour; his pet tortoise walks 1/4 km in 1 hour

maths_rules: 2/5 hour is twice 1/5 hour, so 2 × 3/5 = 6/5 km
the slip: 2/15 is smaller than 3/5, the distance of one fifth of an hour
video_script.design: One idea: cut the whole into equal parts, then take as many parts as the top number says. The line from zero to three kilometres is the anchor and stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a line from zero to 3 km marked 1 hour; a question mark near 2/5 of the hour

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.walk: the line from zero to three kilometres is marked for one hour
marks.ask: a question mark appears near two fifths of the hour

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about Laksh.
<bookmark mark='walk'/>Laksh can walk three kilometres in one hour.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How far can Laksh walk in two fifths of an hour?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the line from zero to 3 km is the whole hour; the hour is cut into five equal parts, and each part is one fifth of an hour

marks.line: the line for one whole hour is drawn
marks.cut: the hour is cut into five equal parts
marks.part: one part lights up as one fifth of an hour

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>This line from zero to three kilometres shows one whole hour.
<bookmark mark='cut'/>Cut the hour into five equal parts.
<bookmark mark='part'/>Each part is one fifth of an hour.

marks.given: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Laksh walks three kilometres in one hour.

beats.on_screen: To find: distance in 2/5 of an hour

marks.find: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the distance in two fifths of an hour.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: distance in 1/5 hour = 3 km ÷ 5 = 3/5 km

marks.one: the line for one fifth of an hour is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, find the distance in one fifth of an hour.
<bookmark mark='div'/>One fifth of an hour is one of five equal parts, so divide three kilometres by five.
Three divided by five is three fifths of a kilometre.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 2/5 hour = 2 × 1/5 hour, so distance = 2 × 3/5 km

marks.twice: two parts of one fifth of an hour are shown together

narration: <bookmark mark='twice'/>Step two, two fifths of an hour is twice one fifth of an hour.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>The time is two times as long, so multiply the distance by two.
We write two times three fifths of a kilometre.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Two times three is six, so we get six fifths.
Laksh can walk six fifths of a kilometre in two fifths of an hour.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>That is one and one fifth kilometres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 2/15 km is written and crossed out; the line shows 3/5 km already covered in one fifth of an hour, far more than 2/15 km

marks.fix: the 3/5 km mark for one fifth of an hour lights up and 2/15 is crossed out
marks.rule: the divide by five step and the multiply by two step glow in turn

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is two fifteenths of a kilometre.
Keeko multiplied five by three at the bottom and kept the two on top.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But two fifteenths of a kilometre is a tiny distance.
One fifth of an hour already gives three fifths of a kilometre.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Two fifths of an hour must give more. Divide three by the bottom number five first. Then multiply by the top number two.
